entities.name: Nonspecific arm pain
observations: Clinical construct generally denotes arm pain without objective findings or correspondence to an objective pathophysiologic process; it may still involve heterogeneous biological and psychosocial contributors. [source: call_I8lKQHCpWROiCvDAuuu5HWwX]

In a retrospective cohort of 634 patients with isolated nonspecific upper-extremity pain, 1 patient (0.16%) had definite symptom-corresponding discrete pathology successfully treated surgically; other diagnoses were possible or speculative and explained only a fraction of symptoms. [source: call_i7bcqTmDXp2uFwba1kLDCS5n]

A community diagnostic study identified 176 patients with only nonspecific arm pain versus 250 with one or more specific upper-limb disorders within a selected examined symptomatic subgroup; this is not a general prevalence estimate. [source: call_nlwlBrP3T0NIMkzzh0pieY0a]

Mechanism-focused studies found heterogeneous sensory or neuropathic classifications rather than a consistent discrete lesion; samples were small and cross-sectional. [sources: call_jM6ZOF7ejNSwMYg8b3YUmrpy, call_MR950Ff6K4KvX4jAlI3LKBxy]
A small EMG study found smaller motor-unit potentials, but causality and a specific myopathy or neuropathy were not established. [source: call_vimIj3KkY6FpsJnJh09Rezfc]

entities.name: Rare discrete pathology
observations: Among 634 patients initially classified with nonspecific upper-extremity pain, definite symptom-corresponding discrete pathology was found in 1 patient (0.16%) during subsequent in-system evaluation. [source: call_i7bcqTmDXp2uFwba1kLDCS5n]

entities.name: Mechanism heterogeneity
observations: Sensory testing and neuropathic-pain classification studies in small nonspecific arm-pain samples showed heterogeneous or discordant patterns, supporting possible sensitization or altered processing rather than one discrete lesion. [sources: call_jM6ZOF7ejNSwMYg8b3YUmrpy, call_MR950Ff6K4KvX4jAlI3LKBxy]
